ideas.description: Exploit, cheapening the per-step Muon cost (~2 ms/step of GPU time per the E018 profile, the same at 24 and 32 px). On the E021 incumbent (2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 with lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655, CUDA-graphed step, 5 epochs at 24 px + 5.75 at 32 px, 0.7552 @ 7.62 s), replace the 3-step Newton-Schulz with Turbo-Muon-style almost-orthogonal preconditioning followed by 2 NS steps (C0008/C0009). Before NS, rescale X's columns by 1/sqrt of the row sums of |X^T X|, inside the batched NS call. Keep the same NS coefficients for the 2 remaining steps, and keep lr, momentum and everything else fixed. Recapture both CUDA graphs in build. Log ms/step per phase.
ideas.expected: Muon time drops by about 0.3-0.45 ms/step over ~344 steps, so train time falls by about 0.1-0.15 s (-1.3 to -2%), to about 7.47-7.52 s. With preconditioning the accuracy change should be within ±0.15 pp of 0.7552, which is inside trajectory noise. Keep it if accuracy is >=0.7535 and time is >=1% lower. If accuracy drops by >0.25 pp, the 3rd NS step matters in this short schedule; close the NS-step axis.

ideas.description: Exploit and test the untested intermediate-resolution step. On E021, change the resolution schedule from 5x24 px + 5.75x32 px to 5x24 px + 2x28 px + 4x32 px (11 epochs in total), with the LR schedule (triangle plus Lookahead) defined over total steps. Use whole augmented images downscaled with bilinear F.interpolate, as for 24 px, and keep AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in the head. Batch 1536 with drop_last at all three shapes. Capture and warm up a third CUDA graph (28 px) in build so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Log per-phase ms/step.
ideas.expected: 28 px epochs cost about 0.66-0.70 s (77% of the pixels; 24 px cost 64% of a full epoch at 56% of the pixels). Time is about 2.7 + 1.37 + 3.38 + 0.06 = about 7.5 s (-1 to -2.5%). Accuracy is 0.753-0.757, centred near 0.755: about 9.45 full-epoch equivalents, the same as the incumbent. Keep it if it is >=0.7535 and faster. If it lands >=0.756, the next step is to move one more 32 px epoch to 28 px.

ideas.description: Explore, following C0012 (EfficientNetV2: scale regularization with image size). On E021 at a fixed epoch schedule, weaken regularization only in the 24 px phase. Use label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 and crop translation of 1 px instead of 2, applied before downscaling, during epochs 1-5. The 32 px phase stays at ls 0.3 and 2 px translate. Pass the ls value through the CUDA graph as a GPU scalar tensor, or capture the low-res graph with its own constant, so nothing is recaptured in the timed region. Time should be unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy +0.1 to +0.25 pp, to about 0.756-0.758. Weaker regularization should let the short, under-trained low-res phase fit faster, while the full-res phase still applies ls 0.3. Since the E020/E021 trajectory noise is ~0.15-0.2 pp, only a gain >=0.2 pp counts as support. In that case, spend it on -0.25 full-res epoch (about -0.2 s). A drop of >=0.15 pp refutes the per-phase-regularization idea here.

ideas.description: Exploit, rebasing the next group-1 cut onto the resizing incumbent. On E021, reduce group 1 from 2 convs to 1: keep the 32x32 whitening-output -> 128 conv followed by pool/BN/GELU, and remove the remaining 16x16 128->128 conv with its BN/GELU. Add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (5x24 + 6.25x32) to compensate. Recapture both graphs in build. In the smoke test, also record a one-step torch.profiler breakdown per stage: conv kernels vs BN/activation/pool kernels, at both 24 and 32 px. This tests H2.4.1.
ideas.expected: Per-step time -8 to -10% in both phases (as E009's 9%), so time is about 7.62 x 0.91 + 0.42 = about 7.3-7.45 s (-2 to -4%). Accuracy 0.7505-0.757: a -0.3 to -0.7 pp cut cost, larger than E009's because no 16x16 conv remains, offset by about +0.45 pp from the extra half epoch. It wins only if it is >=0.7535 at <=7.5 s. The profiler should show >=40% of GPU time in non-conv kernels at 32x32/16x16; if it shows <30%, H2.4's memory-bandwidth mechanism is weakened.

ideas.description: Noise calibration on the current incumbent, with no recipe change. Add an internal salt to the data-order/augmentation generator (the trial seeds stay 0, 1, 2) and run E021 with salt=1. Compare against E021's 0.7552 (salt 0) and log per-seed accuracies. This replaces I028, which was calibrated on E018, now superseded. The margin on the current tip (+0.22 pp) is the binding constraint for every remaining time cut.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±1%). 3-seed mean in 0.753-0.758. A |delta| >=0.2 pp means sub-0.2 pp effects (A28 px stage, NS-step cut, ls per phase) must be treated as inconclusive, and a >=0.755 margin is required before keeping a time cut. If |delta| <=0.1 pp, 0.7535 is an acceptable keep bar. If the salted mean is <0.753, the incumbent's feasibility is fragile and the next kept change must add margin.

ideas.description: Explore an untested H1.7 component: airbench94_muon's per-step weight renormalization. On E021, after each Muon update, rescale every Muon-managed conv weight so each output filter's norm stays at its value at init (or at sqrt(fan_in)-scaled unit norm, as in airbench94_muon). This keeps the effective LR constant under BN scale-invariance. Implement it as one foreach norm/mul inside the CUDA-graphed step and keep weight decay on the Muon group unchanged. Keep lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, Lookahead, the triangle and the resolution schedule fixed.
ideas.expected: Time +0 to +0.5% (one fused foreach op). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.3 pp, with a weak prior toward +0.1 to +0.2 pp, because the effective step size no longer shrinks as filter norms grow. If the gain is >=0.2 pp, keep it and trade it for -0.25 full-res epoch. If the drop is >=0.2 pp, the norm growth is doing useful implicit LR decay alongside the triangle; close this component of H1.7.

drop.reason: Built on E018, which is no longer the incumbent. E020/E021 added progressive resizing, so the epoch compensation and expected times are stale. It is replaced by a rebased group-1 1-conv idea on E021 that keeps the profiler check for H2.4.1.
Noise calibration against E018 (0.7571), which is no longer the tip. It is replaced by the same salt test on the E021 incumbent, where the margin (+0.22 pp) actually binds keep decisions.

structured_output.summary:
The incumbent is E021: progressive resizing (5 epochs at 24 px + 5.75 at 32 px), a 2/3/3 net, Muon at batch 1536 and a CUDA-graphed step, giving 0.7552 @ 7.62 s with only +0.22 pp of margin. Epoch trims and the batch axis are closed, so I'm proposing per-step cuts that keep accuracy, plus margin-building tweaks:
- Turbo-Muon preconditioning with 2 Newton-Schulz steps (H2.5, about -1.5%).
- A 24/28/32 px three-stage schedule (H2.3.1, about -1.5 to -2.5%).
- Lighter regularization in the 24 px phase only, per EfficientNetV2 (H2.3, +0.1-0.25 pp to spend on epochs).
- Cutting group 1 to 1 conv with +0.5 epoch, rebased onto E021, with a profiler check of H2.4.1.
- A salted noise replicate on E021 (H4.1.1).
- An explore run of airbench94_muon weight renormalization (H1.7).

I027 and I028 are dropped because they were tied to the superseded E018 base; their rebased versions are among the ideas above.
